title: Reserve-to-Responsive: Priority-aware reserved pools & soft-fallback autoscale roadmap
creator: Asha Patel
description: Quarterly roadmap and playbook to transition Reserved Pools from a flat reservation model to a priority-aware 'Reserve-to-Responsive' system with soft-fallback autoscale lanes. The initiative reduces customer-facing disruption during spikes while improving utilization and predictable economics for committed customers. Deliverables include product contracts (APIs/config), control-plane policy primitives, console UX for pool priorities and SLAs, and an autoscale policy library with test harnesses.
background: Customers with reserved capacity want both predictable throughput for critical routes and cost efficiency for bulk workloads. Current Dedicated pools are all-or-nothing: when capacity saturates, lower-priority requests fail or are throttled without graceful degradation. Engineering has prototype primitives for priority tagging and preemptible bucketized slots (ENG-5219). This program formalizes roadmap, success metrics, rollout plan, and runbooks for SRE/CS.
goals:
1) Implement priority-aware allocation so critical routes maintain latency SLOs under contention.
2) Add soft-fallback autoscale lanes (burst reservoirs + best-effort preemptibles) to avoid hard failures.
3) Surface priority controls and cost trade-offs in Console.
4) Validate with pilot customers and reduce P99 latency regressions by >= 40% for P0 routes during spikes.
5) Achieve >= 8% improvement in average GPU utilization across targeted pools without increasing tail latency for high-priority traffic.
success_metrics:
- P0 route P99 latency under spike: <= 2x baseline
- Failure-to-complete incidents for reserved customers: 0 during pilot
- Pool utilization uplift: +8% (measured weighted by committed spend)
- Cost per 1k tokens for burst traffic: <=10% over baseline
- Pilot NPS >= 8/10 from dedicated customers testing the feature
scope_included:
- Priority tagging on per-route/per-token basis
- Control-plane policy: reserve, soft-reserve, preemptible buckets, fallback routing
- Console: priority assignment UI, SLA visualization, forecast simulator
- SDK/API: new params for call-time priority and fallback hints
- Autoscale policy library and chaos-scenario tests
out_of_scope:
- Major networking/VPC changes (will integrate with existing Private flow)
- Re-architecting serving runtime kernels for new model types (handled by separate infra initiatives)
- Billing model overhaul (billing team will adopt changes after pilot)

risks_and_mitigations:
- Risk: Priority enforcement may increase complexity of scheduling leading to unforeseen contention. Mitigation: limit initial rollout to small percentage of pools and add circuit breakers.
- Risk: Cost for burst reservoirs spikes unexpectedly. Mitigation: budget guardrails + pre-approved surge caps per customer.
- Risk: Console UX might cause misconfiguration. Mitigation: default safe presets and an in-console simulator before apply.
- Risk: Customer confusion about billing for soft-fallback. Mitigation: clear billing doc + pilot contract addendum.

rollout_plan:
Phase 0: Internal canary on non-customer test clusters (0.5 weeks).
Phase 1: Two enterprise pilots with staggered pools and explicit SLAs (2 weeks).
Phase 2: Gradual ramp to 20% of Dedicated customers with opt-in UI and default safe preset (4 weeks).
Phase 3: GA with account-level controls and billing adjustments (post-pilot, dependent on finance sign-off).
post_launch_runbook:
- Monitor key metrics dashboard (latency by priority, utilization, surge spend)
- If P0 latency > threshold: automatically reduce non-critical preemptible allocations and notify SRE.
- If burst spend exceeds cap: throttle new burst reservations and open billing notification to customer.
- Weekly retrospective in first month and monthly thereafter.
